name: @reticlehq/server
description: Reticle bridge + MCP server. Hosts the browser WS endpoint and exposes MCP tools to the coding agent.

scripts.prepack: node ../scripts/prepare-dist.mjs --clean dist && tsc -b --force && node ../scripts/alias-dist.mjs && node ../scripts/prepare-dist.mjs dist && node ../scripts/stamp-issuer-key.mjs && node ../scripts/pack-docs.mjs

author: Reticle contributors

reticle.changelog: Reticle writes and tightens your regression flows for you: every drive is recorded automatically and replays with no model in the loop. The agent now sees nine tools instead of seventeen, `init` stops at a connected app and proving a flow is a separate first run, and Windows is supported. Upgrading from 2.x: see MIGRATION.md.
breakingChanges: The default MCP surface is the merged nine. reticle_snapshot/query/inspect/state -> reticle_look { action }, reticle_network/console -> reticle_observe { action }, reticle_sessions/feedback -> reticle_session { action }, reticle_wait_for -> reticle_assert { action: "wait" }, reticle_act_sequence -> reticle_act { steps }. Old names redirect when CALLED, but an allowedTools allowlist or an MCP permission rule naming one refuses first -- update those by hand.

Twelve tools are unreachable on the default surface and have NO redirect: reticle_capabilities, reticle_clock, reticle_context, reticle_flow_replay, reticle_flow_save, reticle_intent, reticle_network_mock, reticle_record, reticle_run, reticle_screenshot, reticle_storage, reticle_visual_diff. The default surface ships no reticle_run hatch. Start the daemon with RETICLE_ADVERTISE_ALL_TOOLS=1 (read once at startup) and call them by name. Saved flows still replay via reticle_verify { action: "flows" }.

`reticle init` no longer drives: it ends at a connected session. --flow, --no-drive and --drive-model now exit non-zero, each naming its replacement. Prove a flow with reticle_verify { action: "explore", persona: "<who does what>" }, or npx @reticlehq/server verify <url> --explore --persona "...". init's exit code now means "nothing connected" rather than "no verdict". --files-only is unchanged.
@reticlehq/server, @reticlehq/init and @reticlehq/test declare license FSL-1.1-ALv2 instead of "SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE". The terms are identical; add the SPDX id to a licence allowlist.
